home.quote: Why are we trying to colonize other planets when we are not able to take care of our own?
home.lead: UraqiVision turns NISAR radar data into clear maps, figures and stories, in Spanish and English.

unseen.title: Unseen
unseen.body: Land clearing fires come with thick smoke and the rains with clouds: optical satellites miss exactly the critical moments.

notUnderstood.title: Not understood
notUnderstood.body: Radar does see through smoke and clouds, but its data arrives in technical formats out of reach for most people.

scattered.title: Out of reach
scattered.body: The information is scattered across bulletins, viewers and studies, with no place that brings it together with recent satellite data.

earth.body: NISAR, the NASA–ISRO radar mission, observes the whole Earth every 12 days in L-band, seeing through smoke and clouds.

southAmerica.title: The 2026 fires
southAmerica.body: In Bolivia, the 2026 fires affected 1.25 million hectares up to 11 October; in 2024 they exceeded 10 million.
southAmerica.source: Source: Vice Ministry of Civil Defence, via Correo del Sur (27 Oct 2026).
southAmerica.fact2: On 21 July 2026, San Ignacio de Velasco was the municipality with the most heat spots in the country: 735 of 2,835.

story.title: Where did the vegetation signal drop, and what else agrees?
story.lead: We measure, compare and say where the measurement runs out. We do not confirm causes.

s1.title: First, this place's normal
s1.body: Median HV of {{dates}}, before the change. Light is forest with structure; dark is clearing, pasture or soil.
s1.short: NISAR radar · before the change. Bright = forest · Dark = pasture, soil or cleared land.

s2.title: Then, how it changed by {{date}}
s2.body: That date minus the normal. Brown: the signal dropped; blue: it rose; white: it barely moved. Across most of the landscape the change stays between {{lo}} and {{hi}} dB.
s2.short: After − before. Brown = lost vegetation · Blue = gained · White = no change.

s3.title: Only the strong changes
s3.body: {{n}} patches of at least 1 ha where HV fell more than {{thr}} dB and stayed low on the next date: {{ha}} ha (range {{min}}–{{max}}). These are radar signals, not fire perimeters.
s3.short: Strong drop · ≥ 1 ha · it stays. {{n}} areas · {{ha}} ha ({{min}}–{{max}}). Color = possible cause, not confirmed.

s4.title: A second satellite to cross-check
s4.body: Sentinel-2 between {{from}} and {{to}}. Brown: vegetation lost; green: greener.
s4.brackets: Its dates bracket the radar period.
s4.notBrackets: Its dates do not fully match the radar's.
s4.short: Sentinel-2 images · {{from}} → {{to}}. Checks the radar. Brown = lost vegetation · Green = regrew.

s5.title: Agreement, and where it breaks
s5.body: How much of each optical class the radar flagged. Unchanged land should stay close to zero.
s5.fires: {{a}} of {{b}} hotspots in the period fall on or next to a patch.

serie.title: The whole series
serie.body: The band is the landscape's normal range on each date (10 % to 90 % of pixels). The lines are the median of each patch class. A gap is a date with no usable image.

control.title: Proposal: control zones
control.body: Areas of about 100 ha that resemble what later lost structure, but with no fire and no optical change. If HV also moves there, that movement is seasonal and is subtracted.
criteria: Similar vegetation: median HV within ±1.5 dB of what fell ({{ref}} dB).
No hotspots within 2 km over the whole period, and more than 1 km from any patch and from the edge.
No moderate or severe optical burn (dNBR < 0.27); at least 5 km between zones.
control.found: {{n}} blocks qualify; the {{k}} most similar are proposed.
control.zone: {{id}}: {{ha}} ha, HV {{hv}} dB, nearest hotspot {{km}} km away
control.effect: What changes if they are used
control.hectares: Hectares by {{date}}: without control zones {{now}}; with zones and calibrated thresholds {{ctrl}}.
control.noZones: No block meets the criteria in this box.
control.bodyApplied: Areas of about 100 ha that resemble what later lost structure, with no fire and no optical change. Whatever HV did there is seasonal and is subtracted across the box.
control.calibration: Thresholds calibrated with these zones and with Sentinel-2 (MC-03): {{s}} / {{c}} / {{e}} dB, the least strict values that flag at most 2 %, 1 % and 0.5 % of the area where Sentinel-2 sees no change.
control.falseAlarm: With the sensitive threshold, {{pct}} % of the area with no optical change ends up flagged, and {{ctrl}} % of the control zones.

limits.linea_base_2_fechas: The baseline uses 2 dates, not 3 (MC-02): before the data gap there is no sound image on this orbit.
limits.quemado_antes_de_la_serie: Anything burned before {{start}} was already burned in the baseline: the radar cannot see it as change.
limits.umbrales_sin_calibrar: The thresholds are not yet calibrated with control zones.
limits.optico_fuera_de_periodo: The Sentinel-2 images do not bracket the radar period.
limits.producto_provisional: NISAR PROVISIONAL: calibrated, but not yet fully validated by the mission.
limits.optico_con_fenologia: The optical witness includes seasonal vegetation changes (leaf fall, regrowth), which are not fire.
limits.revision_visual_pendiente: A visual review of a sample of patches is still missing (VC-05).
limits.procedencia_incompleta: An original file checksum is missing (CQ-06).

validated.title: VALIDATED segment (separate)
validated.note: Product with the mission's full validation, published since 21 Oct 2026. Shown separately: it does not enter the baseline, the change or the hectares (RN-02).
